PART 8 / Evaluation, scale and operating the company
CHAPTER 71

Incident runbooks for a search platform

A runbook should say what to protect, what to stop and how to prove that recovery actually worked.

Runbook: crawl pressure harms an origin

Protect the external site first. Reduce concurrency, stop optional rendering and respect the relevant retry behavior. Inspect per-origin requests, redirect expansion, robots freshness and task duplication. A global crawl-rate chart can hide a severe local overload. Resume gradually using observed latency and error recovery rather than immediately draining the accumulated queue.

Do not solve a blocked origin by moving requests through more addresses to evade its limits. The engineering objective is cooperative acquisition, not bypassing a publisher's controls.

Runbook: stale or missing results

Determine whether the failure is discovery, acquisition, extraction, indexing, publication, retrieval or policy. Compare the latest accepted observation to the published manifest and the query's pinned generation. A healthy crawler does not imply a fresh index. A fresh index does not imply that a document is eligible or relevant to the specific query.

If a publication is incomplete, keep the previous valid generation while repairing the staged one. Do not change the pointer to a partially built release merely to reduce the freshness metric. Track affected corpus slices and user-visible freshness separately from batch completion.

Runbook: relevance regression

Freeze the rollout and preserve the exact model, feature, tokenizer and index identifiers. Compare matched query slices against the prior configuration. Separate retrieval recall loss from reranker ordering changes and results-page composition. A rollback must restore a compatible set, not only the model binary. Continue enforcing current safety and removal policies during rollback.

Runbook: a removed result reappears

Treat this as an authority failure, not just a cache miss. Identify every serving surface, invalidate dependent outputs and check policy revision propagation. Inspect restored snapshots, secondary indexes, generated answers and administrative bypasses. Recovery is complete only when probes using old generations are also denied and the reason is observable.

Runbook: tail latency and overload

Reject low-priority work early, reduce optional retrieval branches and preserve critical lexical service where possible. Use remaining deadline, queue depth and concurrency limits to choose fallback behavior. Disable uncontrolled hedging before it amplifies load. Report partial coverage honestly; do not label an incomplete shard result as an exhaustive search.

Runbook: unsafe or unsupported generated answers

Stop the affected synthesis configuration, preserve access-controlled evidence and trace metadata, and fall back to suitable search results. Determine whether the defect arose in retrieval, source eligibility, prompt isolation, synthesis or citation support. A model-only fix is insufficient when the true problem is stale evidence or an incorrect scope join.

Recovery verification

Every runbook ends with probes that exercise the broken invariant, an owner, a rollback condition and a follow-up action. Separate service restoration from root-cause completion. Preserve enough evidence for learning without expanding sensitive-data retention indiscriminately. The most useful incident review identifies which contract permitted the failure and changes that contract or its enforcement.

PART 8 / Evaluation, scale and operating the company
CHAPTER 72

Production readiness and the executable learning path

Local demonstrations explain invariants; production readiness requires evidence across concurrency, scale, security and real operations.

Read, run, modify

The companion lab is deliberately small enough to inspect. Start with tokenization and positional postings, reproduce the BM25 example, then compare exhaustive scoring against safe block-bound pruning. Change the document distribution and block size. Observe that an optimization can be correct yet save little work on an unfavorable corpus.

Next run PageRank on a graph with dangling and disconnected nodes. Check non-negativity and normalization rather than memorizing one ranking. Combine two ranked lists with reciprocal rank fusion and inspect how duplicates and ties are handled. These exercises expose assumptions that disappear in architecture slides.

Follow the control plane

Exercise crawl epochs, observation versions, generation publication, policy tombstones and outbox deduplication. Delay an older worker until after a newer observation commits. Lose the response after a generation pointer changes. Query an old snapshot after removal. The required behavior follows from the authority rules, not from the order in which network messages happen to arrive.

The local model uses SQLite transactions and does not implement a replicated consensus system. Its tests can establish selected behavior of this implementation under its local concurrency model. They cannot establish cross-region safety, global clock guarantees or the correctness of an unrelated production database.

Retrieval gates

Before launch, maintain a judged query set, an exact retrieval baseline, multilingual slices, rare-entity queries and adversarial examples. Measure recall before the final reranker. Verify that versioned tokenizers, features and embeddings match their indexes. Test tie behavior and numeric assumptions in every pruning optimization.

Serving gates

Demonstrate bounded deadlines, overload fallback, safe cell evacuation, immutable release publication and dependency-aware cache invalidation. Measure recovery against the current policy overlay. A generation rollback must never undo a removal. Capacity tests should include correlated hot keys and simultaneous slow shards, not only independent uniform traffic.

Trust and AI gates

Verify fetcher isolation, administrative authorization, data scope propagation, retention, deletion and sensitive-log controls. For generated answers, distinguish valid references from supported claims. Evaluate citation freshness, conflicts, source withdrawal and prompt injection. An action-taking feature needs explicit consent and a durable outcome model beyond the read-only search path.

Operational gates

Assign owners and on-call coverage, rehearse incident procedures and document every degraded mode. Establish publisher-support processes and explain what notifications, inspections and analytics do and do not guarantee. Review applicable legal and commercial requirements with qualified specialists before operating on real data.

The final mental model

A search engine is a set of coordinated evidence-processing systems. Crawling observes, indexing organizes, ranking estimates usefulness, policy determines eligibility and presentation communicates a result. AI synthesis adds another inference layer; it does not remove the need for the others. The strongest design keeps those boundaries explicit and makes every important decision traceable to versions, evidence and authority.

The appendices translate that model into schemas, API contracts, algorithms, test specifications and a reproducible local lab. They are a starting implementation vocabulary, not a claim to reproduce Google's private source code or its production service guarantees.

APPENDIX A

Logical data model and storage contracts

How to use this model

These 48 entities form a proposed logical model, not a claim about Google tables. A production system may combine or split them. Each entity exists because its authority, retention, consistency or access pattern differs from another. Do not implement every table before the first useful product; preserve the boundaries even when several share one database.

The local teaching lab implements only ten SQLite tables. Its simple policy boolean represents a removal gate, not the full surface-specific policy model described in the chapters. It does not implement property verification, administrative authentication, a network crawler, browser sandboxing or a distributed database.

Acquisition

Entity Logical key Contract
Origin origin_id Scheme, host and port; owns politeness and robots state. Do not merge unrelated origins by registrable domain alone.
OriginLease origin_id, epoch Bounded acquisition authority. A newer epoch fences late workers; time is supplied by the authority, not arbitrary clients.
RobotsSnapshot origin_id, revision Fetched policy body, status, expiry and parser version. Preserve the decision used for an attempted request.
URLIdentity url_id Lossless normalized URL and original spelling. Keep transformation provenance; never strip meaningful parameters blindly.
DiscoveryEdge source_id, target_id Link or feed observation with time and provenance; discovery does not imply crawl permission or trust.
FrontierTask task_id URL, priority, due time and retry budget. Deduplicate equivalent work while retaining independent evidence.
FetchAttempt attempt_id Lease epoch, request chain, response classification and timing. An attempt can fail without changing the current observation.
ResponseObject content_hash Immutable fetched bytes and validated size. Content-addressed identity does not grant serving permission.
RenderJob render_id Input observation, browser version and resource budget. Completion is separate from successful initial HTML fetch.
RenderedSnapshot render_id, revision DOM, visible text and resource outcomes. Missing resources remain explicit instead of silently becoming an empty page.

Documents

Entity Logical key Contract
Document doc_id Stable logical identity with current accepted observation pointer. URL changes and canonical clusters need separate identities.
Observation doc_id, sequence Immutable source revision plus extraction inputs. An older scheduled observation cannot overwrite a newer accepted one.
Extraction observation_id, extractor Fields, links and language candidates bound to source bytes and parser version; preserve extraction failures.
Passage observation_id, passage_id Text offsets, heading path and hash. Citations resolve to this evidence unit, not merely a domain.
CanonicalCluster cluster_id, revision Proposed equivalence set and selected representative. Similarity does not transfer ownership or authorization.
CanonicalMembership cluster_id, doc_id Versioned evidence for membership; changes must invalidate dependent deduplication and canonical projections.
PolicyDecision doc_id, revision Current surface-specific eligibility and reason. Removal authority must remain stronger than an old content snapshot.
PublisherPreference property_id, revision Explicit crawl, preview or AI-surface preference, effective time, scope and authorized actor.
RemovalCase case_id Authority, affected scope, audit trail, decision and appeal state. Collection minimization applies to supporting evidence.

Indexes

Entity Logical key Contract
IndexGeneration generation_id Immutable manifest for a compatible corpus view. States progress from staged to validated to published.
IndexSegment segment_id Checksummed postings and dictionaries with tokenizer and schema identifiers. Never mutate a published segment in place.
SegmentMembership generation_id, segment_id Manifest edges describing the exact searchable snapshot; reference counts inform safe garbage collection.
TermDictionary segment_id, term Encoded term and postings address. Lookup correctness depends on normalization and format version.
PostingBlock term_id, block_id Document gaps, frequencies, positions and safe score metadata. Bounds must dominate the actual score used for pruning.
ForwardDocument generation_id, doc_id Stored fields and offsets needed after candidate retrieval. Pin to the same generation as the candidate.
LinkGraphSnapshot graph_generation Versioned nodes and links for graph computations. Preserve dangling nodes and provenance of edge filtering.
FeatureSnapshot feature_set, as_of Point-in-time features with schema and entity joins. Training must not read values from the future.
EmbeddingGeneration model_id, generation Vectors, dimensions, normalization and tokenizer contract. Query and document encoders must be compatible.
PublishPointer corpus_id Current generation and writer epoch. Update conditionally and retain a durable publication receipt.
PublishReceipt operation_id Request digest and committed result. A lost acknowledgment is resolved by reading the receipt, not repeating blindly.

Serving

Entity Logical key Contract
QueryRequest request_id Scope, locale, budget and configuration IDs. Retain only what observability and approved analytics require.
QueryPlan request_id, revision Branches, shard selection, deadline and degradation policy. Do not hide partial coverage from downstream stages.
CandidateSet branch_id Document or passage IDs, generation and scores. These are proposals, not final eligibility decisions.
RankingDecision request_id, stage Model, feature version and ordering outcome. Separate retrieval recall from reranker quality.
ResultsLayout request_id Composed modules with deduplication and safety constraints. Advertisements retain distinct eligibility and labeling.
AnswerArtifact answer_id Claim set, model version, scope and dependencies. A cached answer remains invalid when required evidence is withdrawn.
CitationReference answer_id, citation_id Immutable evidence reference and claim mapping. Existence and semantic support are different validations.
CacheDependency artifact_id, dependency Document, policy, model or scope dependency used to invalidate outputs without assuming a universal cache lifetime.
ActionIntent action_id Proposed external side effect, consent and request digest. Search evidence alone cannot authorize a purchase or booking.

Operations

Entity Logical key Contract
OutboxEvent event_id Committed state-change notification stored with the authoritative update; at-least-once delivery remains expected.
ConsumerReceipt consumer_id, event_id Deduplication record committed with the consumer effect. A broker acknowledgment alone cannot ensure effect uniqueness.
Judgment query_id, doc_id, version Human relevance label with rubric and assessor metadata. Labels support evaluation rather than directly setting live rank.
ExperimentAssignment unit_id, experiment_id Stable assignment and eligibility. Avoid using post-treatment behavior to redefine the comparison population.
MetricDefinition metric_id, revision Event semantics, denominator and late-data policy. A dashboard number without its definition is not reproducible.
ModelRelease model_id, revision Weights, training lineage, evaluation, feature dependencies and rollback compatibility.
ServiceObjective service_id, revision SLI definition, target, window and degradation contract. These are proposed objectives, not Google SLAs.
AuditEvent audit_id Actor, operation, authorization context and result. Restrict access and avoid unnecessary sensitive payloads.
PropertyOwnership property_id, principal Verified publisher scope and delegated rights. Revocation must affect subsequent privileged operations.

Physical design decisions

Partition high-volume observations by stable document identity and time, but keep each authoritative pointer update within a transaction that can enforce its invariant. Place large immutable bytes outside the metadata transaction and publish their references only after validation. Unreferenced temporary objects are a garbage-collection concern; half-published authoritative pointers are a correctness defect.

Use unique constraints for receipts and business identities. A background repair process is not a replacement for an enforceable uniqueness rule. Index the actual access paths: due frontier tasks by origin, current policy by document, generation membership by generation, and consumer receipts by consumer plus event. Protect administrative indexes from becoming a side channel into private documents.

Representative local transaction

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
UPDATE publication
   SET generation = :new_generation
 WHERE singleton = 1 AND epoch = :epoch
   AND generation IS :expected_generation;
-- Require exactly one matched row after validating the manifest.
INSERT INTO receipts VALUES (:scope, :op, :digest, :result);
INSERT INTO outbox(kind, entity, payload)
VALUES ('published', :new_generation, :result);
COMMIT;

The complete runnable schema is in lab/schema.sql. The snippet omits the code's receipt lookup and validation checks for readability. SQLite's local serialization does not demonstrate quorum replication or failure safety across regions.

APPENDIX B

Proposed API contracts and operation semantics

Proposed endpoints, not Google APIs

The paths below belong to the fictional Atlas reference design. They are not callable Google endpoints. Actual Google publisher API boundaries are described in Chapter 68 and the source registry. Production authorization, quotas, transport security and field validation are required even where the table emphasizes only the consistency contract.

Endpoint Caller Required information Outcome contract
POST /v1/frontier/requests Verified publisher or discovery service URL, property, reason, operation ID Accepted task reference; not a guarantee of fetch, indexing or rank.
POST /v1/origins/{id}/leases Scheduler Expected ownership state, lease duration Monotonic epoch and expiry; reject overlapping authority.
POST /v1/observations Authorized crawler Origin epoch, sequence, content hash, operation ID Committed observation receipt; stale workers cannot replace newer content.
POST /v1/renders Processing service Observation ID, renderer version, budget Durable job ID; separate accepted, running, complete and failed states.
POST /v1/generations Indexer Manifest, corpus, tokenizer, schemas, model IDs Immutable staged generation; cannot serve until validated.
POST /v1/generations/{id}/validate Release service Checksums, compatibility evidence, validation revision Validation result; a checksum alone does not establish semantic quality.
POST /v1/publications Publisher service Expected pointer, new generation, epoch, operation ID Committed pointer receipt or explicit conflict.
POST /v1/documents/{id}/policy Authorized policy operator Expected revision, decision, reason, operation ID New policy revision and invalidation event; audited authority required.
POST /v1/search User-facing gateway Query, locale, scope, deadline, allowed features Results plus generation and degradation metadata; no private cross-scope reuse.
POST /v1/evidence Answer planner Candidate IDs, generation, scope, budget Eligible immutable passages and evidence expiry; not a claim of entailment.
POST /v1/answers Answer service Question, evidence set, schema, model, scope Supported claim artifact or bounded fallback; dependencies retained.
POST /v1/actions Explicitly authorized user workflow Intent, consent reference, operation ID Accepted action and outcome state; timeout can mean unknown.
POST /v1/properties/{id}/inspect Verified publisher Owned URL and requested diagnostic fields Timestamped pipeline observations, not guaranteed future inclusion.
POST /v1/properties/{id}/preferences Verified property administrator Expected revision, surface preferences Versioned preference with effective time and propagation status.
POST /v1/events/acknowledge Named consumer Event ID and consumer identity Receipt only after atomic local effect; duplicates return previous result.
GET /v1/operations/{id} Original caller or authorized operator Operation ID within principal scope Durable committed outcome or known pending state; not inferred from silence.

Common write envelope

{
  "operation_id": "publish-000042",
  "expected_generation": "g40",
  "new_generation": "g41",
  "writer_epoch": 12,
  "manifest_hash": "sha256:..."
}

Compute the request digest over canonical semantic fields, not volatile transport headers. Bind the receipt to the caller's authorization scope. Reusing an operation identifier with a different request is a conflict. Retrying an identical authorized request returns its durable outcome even when the original response was lost. Recheck authorization before exposing a receipt; idempotency is not an access-control bypass.

Error taxonomy

Distinguish invalid input, unauthenticated caller, forbidden scope, stale version, exhausted budget, unavailable dependency and unknown external outcome. An empty result set is not interchangeable with a timed-out shard. An accepted job is not a finished job. Include a stable reason code and a trace reference without leaking confidential document contents.

Pagination and read consistency

Pagination tokens should be opaque, authenticated and bound to a generation, query, scope and expiration. Replaying a token under another user or corpus must fail. A long-lived cursor can pin storage and retention, so set bounded lifetimes and preserve current removal checks even while reading an older generation.

Compatibility and evolution

Add optional fields without silently changing the meaning of existing ones. Version tokenization, score definitions and evidence schemas explicitly. A client that does not understand partial coverage must not be given an apparently ordinary response that hides it. Test older clients against new server responses before rollout.

APPENDIX C

Ten critical algorithms

Algorithms are contracts made executable

These ten sketches capture proposed invariants. They omit production details such as distributed consensus, authentication, storage-layout optimization and complete error handling. The companion code implements selected local mechanisms; the remaining sketches are implementation guidance.

C01. Origin lease and guarded observation

A scheduler grants a bounded epoch. The sink verifies epoch, expiry and document sequence in the same transaction as the authoritative update. The authority owns time; the local lab injects it for deterministic tests.

begin transaction
if receipt exists: validate digest; return prior result
require current_origin.epoch == request.epoch
require authority_now < current_origin.lease_until
require request.sequence > document.sequence
write document pointer; preserve current policy
write receipt and outbox event
commit

C02. Generation publication

Stage immutable segments and validate compatibility before touching the public pointer. A committed receipt resolves uncertain acknowledgment. Rollback selects a compatible older content generation but never an older removal authority.

begin transaction
if receipt exists: validate digest; return prior result
require writer_epoch == current_epoch
require pointer == expected_pointer
require manifest is validated and compatible
set pointer = new_generation
write receipt and publication event
commit

C03. Current-policy filtering

A candidate is only a proposal. Apply a current policy decision to every surface that can expose content, including old snapshots and generated evidence. Define an explicit freshness bound for the policy read.

for candidate in pinned_generation:
    policy = current_policy(candidate.document_id)
    if policy is unavailable:
        apply conservative surface-specific fallback
    elif policy.allows(request.surface, request.scope):
        retain candidate
record policy revision used

C04. BM25 candidate scoring

Use generation-pinned corpus statistics. Deduplicate query terms in this lab. This is an understandable lexical reference model, not the recovered Google ranking function.

terms = unique(tokenize(query))
for document in eligible_documents:
    score = 0
    for term in terms:
        idf = log(1 + (N-df[term]+0.5)/(df[term]+0.5))
        K = k1 * (1-b+b*length[document]/average_length)
        score += idf * tf * (k1+1)/(tf+K)
    retain positive scores with stable ties

C05. Safe block-bound pruning

The stored upper bounds cover exactly the nonnegative lexical score used in the local model. They do not cover an unseen neural reranker. Strict comparison preserves ties. Index-building cost is not included in document-score counters.

for block in document_blocks:
    upper = sum(term_block_max[t, block] for t in terms)
    threshold = kth_score if heap_is_full else -infinity
    if upper < threshold:
        skip block
    else:
        score eligible documents exactly
        retain top k ordered by score, then document_id

C06. PageRank with dangling mass

This is the historical graph intuition, not a modern Search ranking specification. Deduplicate outgoing edges and include destination-only nodes. A dangling node redistributes its mass rather than causing it to disappear.

rank[v] = 1/N for every node
repeat until L1 change < tolerance:
    dangling = sum(rank[v] for nodes without outlinks)
    next[v] = (1-d)/N + d*dangling/N
    for edge u -> v:
        next[v] += d*rank[u]/outdegree[u]
    rank = next
require finite nonnegative scores and sum near one

C07. Reciprocal rank fusion

Merge retrieval methods without pretending that their raw scores have the same scale. Remove duplicates within each list and make the tie order deterministic. Fusion is a candidate combination technique, not a policy override.

scores = map with default zero
for ranking in ranked_lists:
    ranking = deduplicate_preserving_order(ranking)
    for rank, document in enumerate(ranking, start=1):
        scores[document] += 1/(constant+rank)
return sort_by_descending_score_then_id(scores)

C08. Atomic consumer deduplication

The consumer receipt and local effect share a transaction. Reprocessing an event after a lost acknowledgment is safe for that local effect. External side effects need their own idempotency and reconciliation contract.

begin transaction
if (consumer, event_id) already recorded:
    return previous outcome
validate event schema and authority
apply local effect
insert (consumer, event_id) receipt
commit
acknowledge broker

C09. Grounded-answer release gate

Structural validation establishes that references exist and are permitted. Semantic support requires separate evaluation; this lab does not automate entailment. Recheck dependencies before releasing an answer that took time to generate.

for claim in draft.claims:
    require cited IDs exist in the evidence set
    require scope, hash, expiry and current policy are valid
    evaluate whether evidence supports the exact claim
    preserve uncertainty or omit unsupported statements
if dependencies changed:
    regenerate within budget or fall back
release versioned answer with dependency manifest

C10. Deadline-aware fanout and degradation

Allocate from one end-to-end budget instead of giving every child a fresh full timeout. Optional work must not consume the reserve needed to compose and return a useful result.

remaining = deadline - authority_now
reserve response_composition_budget
admit only branches affordable within remaining
propagate remaining deadline to every child
cancel obsolete work on completion or timeout
merge responses with explicit coverage metadata
fall back without weakening required policy gates

Testing an algorithm is not testing a product

An exact top-k comparison establishes equivalence only for the implemented score, eligible set and tie rule. A SQLite race establishes behavior only under that database's local transaction model. A citation hash establishes byte identity, not truth. Carry these scope statements into code reviews and test reports so small demonstrations do not become unjustified production assurances.

APPENDIX D

Adversarial test specification: 80 scenarios

Specification, not an execution claim

The 80 scenarios below are a proposed adversarial acceptance program. They are not all implemented or executed in the companion lab. The lab's 67 actual tests cover a narrower local model; Appendix G reports their results and limitations. Network isolation, browser behavior, distributed replication, real authorization and semantic claim support require additional systems and test environments.

For each scenario, record the invariant, injected fault, observable outcome, evidence, responsible owner and recovery action. A test that only checks for a successful HTTP response is insufficient when the failure concerns stale authority or missing coverage.

Acquisition and rendering

T001. An origin lease expires while a fetch is blocked; its late response must not overwrite a newer accepted observation.

T002. Two schedulers race for the same origin; only one unexpired acquisition authority may be granted.

T003. A redirect changes to a private network address; the fetcher must reapply egress validation before connecting.

T004. DNS resolution changes between validation and connection; pin or revalidate the actual destination to prevent rebinding.

T005. A robots request fails transiently; apply the defined fallback and freshness policy rather than silently assuming unrestricted access.

T006. A publisher disallows crawling while a recrawl is queued; admission must evaluate the applicable current policy.

T007. A compressed response expands beyond limits; abort without exhausting shared memory or disk.

T008. A page creates an infinite calendar or parameter space; discovery budgets must prevent unbounded frontier growth.

T009. JavaScript never becomes idle; render completion must use bounded conditions and retain partial-outcome diagnostics.

T010. The initial HTML succeeds but required content requests fail; extraction must not classify missing content as authoritative emptiness.

Document identity and policy

T011. An older observation sequence arrives after a newer one; reject the stale pointer update and preserve its diagnostic receipt.

T012. Two URLs differ by a meaningful query parameter; normalization must not merge their distinct content identities.

T013. A near-duplicate page claims another publisher as canonical; similarity alone must not transfer ownership or permissions.

T014. A document is removed after an index snapshot is built; current eligibility must suppress the snapshot candidate.

T015. A removed URL is rediscovered by a sitemap; discovery must not automatically cancel the administrative decision.

T016. A publisher changes preview restrictions; cached snippets must obey the effective policy contract.

T017. A Search generative-AI preference changes; eligible ordinary results and answer evidence must follow their distinct surface policies.

T018. A property delegate loses access; subsequent privileged inspection or removal operations must fail authorization.

T019. An authorized reinstatement races with removal; compare revisions so neither silently overwrites a newer decision.

T020. A backup predates a tombstone; restoring content must not restore obsolete permission authority.

Index construction and publication

T021. A segment checksum is wrong; validation must prevent publication and identify the corrupt artifact.

T022. A build emits postings with a different tokenizer version; the generation manifest must reject incompatible components.

T023. One shard has not finished staging; a global pointer must not claim that the generation is complete.

T024. A publisher loses its response after commit; retrying the same operation must return the committed generation.

T025. Two publishers use the same expected pointer; only the permitted conditional update may succeed.

T026. An old regional publisher returns after failover; an epoch check must fence it even when it still has credentials.

T027. A crash occurs between metadata change and event creation; the transaction must expose neither a half-update nor a missing event.

T028. Compaction removes an object still referenced by a pinned generation; reference and retention rules must prevent premature deletion.

T029. A new embedding model has different dimensions; querying the old vector index must fail compatibility checks.

T030. A rollback restores a model but not its feature schema; the release system must reject the incompatible combination.

Retrieval and ranking

T031. A rare exact identifier has weak semantic similarity; the hybrid plan must preserve lexical recall for the evaluated query slice.

T032. A query repeats a term; the score must follow the documented query-term policy rather than accidental double counting.

T033. Two documents tie at the top-k threshold; pruning and exhaustive scoring must preserve the same stable ordering.

T034. A bound excludes a positive score component; the optimizer must not use that bound to skip candidates.

T035. Deletions reduce the eligible set; a pruning path must remain equivalent to its filtered exhaustive baseline.

T036. A document contains a repeated phrase; positional matching must handle repeated terms and order correctly.

T037. A graph contains only dangling nodes; PageRank must retain finite normalized mass.

T038. A fusion input repeats a document; the duplicate must not earn multiple contributions from one ranked list.

T039. A feature join reads a future value during training; point-in-time validation must identify the leakage.

T040. A ranker improves average clicks but harms rare-language relevance; rollout decisions must inspect the affected slices.

Serving and caching

T041. A hot query saturates one shard; admission and replication policy must contain the hotspot without unlimited retries.

T042. A shard times out after other shards return; the response must expose the defined partial-coverage behavior.

T043. Optional neural inference exceeds its budget; the system must preserve a useful authorized fallback.

T044. Every slow request triggers a hedge; a shared hedge budget must prevent a positive feedback overload loop.

T045. A cache key omits user scope; tests must detect and reject cross-user private-result reuse.

T046. A cache entry depends on a withdrawn source; policy invalidation must override its remaining time to live.

T047. A pagination token is replayed under another query or scope; authenticated token binding must reject it.

T048. A release changes score semantics without changing the cache namespace; compatibility validation must prevent stale reuse.

T049. A regional loss causes failover traffic plus rebuild traffic; reserve capacity must keep recovery from overwhelming the survivor.

T050. An operator restores an old results cache; current eligibility must still suppress newly removed documents.

Grounded answers and agents

T051. A model emits a citation identifier absent from its evidence set; structural validation must reject the reference.

T052. A valid citation does not support the written claim; support evaluation must flag it despite passing reference checks.

T053. A source changes version during a comparison task; the answer must preserve which version supports each claim.

T054. Two credible sources conflict; synthesis must preserve uncertainty rather than invent an unsupported compromise.

T055. A retrieved page instructs the agent to leak context; the page must remain untrusted evidence, not executable authority.

T056. A private passage enters a public answer cache; scope propagation must block publication or shared reuse.

T057. A cited document is withdrawn during generation; the final release gate must revalidate dependencies.

T058. A query planner recursively expands branches; a global work budget must stop unbounded fanout.

T059. An action request loses its acknowledgment after an external commit; reconciliation must avoid a duplicate side effect.

T060. A user grants read access but not purchase consent; the action gateway must distinguish the two authorities.

Data, evaluation and experimentation

T061. An event is delivered twice; consumer receipts and local effects must commit atomically and avoid duplication.

T062. A consumer crashes after applying an effect but before acknowledgment; retry must resolve through the committed receipt.

T063. A late event changes a daily metric; the analytical contract must define revision and completeness behavior.

T064. An experiment uses post-treatment activity to select users; analysis must identify the biased comparison.

T065. Human judgments use incompatible rubrics; dataset versioning must prevent silent aggregation.

T066. A query has no relevant labeled documents; evaluation must report the chosen undefined-or-zero convention explicitly.

T067. A privacy deletion reaches raw logs but not derived features; lineage must identify downstream cleanup obligations.

T068. A model artifact has no training or evaluation provenance; the release gate must deny promotion.

T069. A dashboard changes its denominator; the metric revision must make historical comparisons explicit.

T070. A logging change captures raw private text; access and minimization checks must catch the regression.

Security and operations

T071. A crawler credential is compromised; revocation and workload isolation must bound access without relying on a browser sandbox alone.

T072. A support operator attempts an unscoped removal; administrative authorization must require appropriate property or case authority.

T073. A key rotates while jobs are in flight; verification must honor a bounded transition without accepting arbitrary old keys.

T074. A malformed index file reaches a serving process; validation and process isolation must contain parser failure.

T075. A deployment removes all replicas of a shard simultaneously; disruption policy must prevent avoidable unavailability.

T076. A cell is declared recovered while policy data is stale; recovery probes must fail the no-resurrection gate.

T077. A dependency outage triggers noisy alerts; incident triage must retain the user-visible symptom and ownership route.

T078. A capacity test uses only uniform traffic; launch review must require skew, correlated failures and cold-cache tests.

T079. A new product uses a source outside its approved scope; governance review must block reuse despite technical accessibility.

T080. An incident is marked resolved after latency recovers; verification must also probe correctness, freshness and removal behavior.

APPENDIX E

Glossary: 80 terms

A compact vocabulary

These definitions describe the proposed design unless a term is explicitly identified as a dated public Google system name. Protocol and product details remain governed by their cited documentation. A term that sounds similar to another often represents a different authority or lifecycle.

Acquisition. The process of discovering and retrieving source material; it does not itself establish indexing eligibility.

Admission control. A decision to accept, reject or defer work before queues and dependencies become overloaded.

AI grounding. Binding generated claims to retrieved evidence with appropriate scope, freshness and support.

Answer dependency. A document, policy, model or scope version whose change can invalidate a generated artifact.

Approximate nearest neighbor. Vector retrieval that trades some exact-neighbor recall for speed or resource efficiency.

Authority. The current right to make a state transition or expose content; distinct from possession of old data.

BM25. A lexical relevance function combining inverse document frequency, term frequency saturation and length normalization.

Block bound. An upper estimate of scores achievable within a postings or document block for safe pruning.

Candidate generation. Fast retrieval of a manageable set for later ranking; missed candidates cannot be recovered by that reranker.

Canonical cluster. A versioned grouping of documents believed to represent equivalent content, with a selected representative.

CAS. Compare-and-swap: change state only when its expected version or value still matches.

Cell. A bounded infrastructure failure domain with deliberate ownership, capacity and recovery behavior.

Citation integrity. The property that a reference resolves to the intended eligible evidence; not identical to semantic support.

Click bias. Distortion caused by position, presentation, selection and user behavior in observed interaction data.

Colossus. Google storage infrastructure described in public accounts; not evidence that every Search component uses one public cloud SKU.

Compaction. Rewriting index or storage segments to consolidate data and remove obsolete entries safely.

Corpus statistics. Generation-specific counts such as document frequency and average length used by a retrieval score.

Crawl budget. The practical allocation of acquisition work under source capacity, scheduling priorities and resource limits.

Crawl frontier. The prioritized, deduplicated collection of pending URL acquisition tasks.

Current-policy overlay. A serving-time eligibility layer that can override older immutable content snapshots.

Dangling node. A graph node with no outgoing links; PageRank needs an explicit rule for its probability mass.

Deadline propagation. Passing the remaining end-to-end time budget to child work instead of resetting a full timeout.

Degradation. A documented smaller operating mode used when resources or dependencies are unavailable.

Document frequency. The number of documents containing a term within the scoring corpus.

Embedding generation. A set of vectors bound to a model, tokenizer, dimensions and normalization contract.

Entailment. Whether evidence actually supports the meaning of a claim; a matching citation ID is insufficient.

Epoch. A monotonically increasing ownership generation used to reject stale writers.

Evidence passage. A bounded source span with document version, offsets and provenance suitable for citation.

Fanout. The number of downstream requests created by one query or operation.

Feature leakage. Use of information in training or evaluation that would not have been available at prediction time.

Fencing. Enforcement at the sink that rejects work from an obsolete owner or epoch.

Forward index. Document-oriented stored fields or token information, complementing term-oriented inverted postings.

Freshness. How closely served information reflects the relevant current source state, under an explicit time model.

Generation manifest. A versioned description of the exact compatible segments, models and schemas in one release.

Ground-truth judgment. A label under a specified rubric; it is evidence for evaluation, not an infallible universal truth.

Hedging. Launching a bounded redundant request to reduce tail latency; uncontrolled hedging can worsen overload.

Host politeness. Rate and concurrency discipline that protects an origin from excessive crawler load.

Hybrid retrieval. Combining lexical and semantic candidate sources while preserving their compatibility and policy contracts.

Idempotency. Returning one durable semantic outcome for repeated equivalent requests within a defined key scope.

Index generation. An immutable, coherent searchable snapshot identified independently of the currently published pointer.

Indexing lag. Delay between an accepted source observation and its availability in a published searchable generation.

Inverted index. A mapping from terms to documents and optionally frequencies, positions and other retrieval metadata.

Lease. Time-bounded authority to perform work; safe use also needs sink enforcement and a clock contract.

Lexical retrieval. Candidate matching based on terms and their statistics rather than only vector similarity.

Live document set. The documents eligible within a particular index view and policy context.

Model compatibility. Agreement between a model and the features, tokenization, vectors and schemas it expects.

Navboost. A name described in dated public Google engineer-call notes for interaction-related ranking information.

nDCG. Normalized discounted cumulative gain: a ranked relevance metric with an explicit gain and discount definition.

Noindex. An indexing directive distinct from a robots crawl prohibition and from authentication.

Observation sequence. An ordering token used to prevent an older accepted-work result from replacing a newer one.

Operation receipt. A durable mapping from scoped request identity and digest to its committed result.

Outbox. An event record committed with a state change so notification can be delivered and retried later.

PageRank. A link-graph probability model; one historical idea within a much broader modern search system.

Passage ranking. Evaluating relevant spans within documents rather than treating every document as one undifferentiated text block.

Point-in-time join. A feature join constrained to values available at the prediction or historical evaluation time.

Policy revision. A versioned eligibility decision that can change independently of stored content and index generation.

Posting. A term-document record, often containing frequency, positions or encoded access metadata.

Precision. The fraction of retrieved items considered relevant under a chosen judgment definition.

Private scope. An access boundary tied to a user or authorized group that must propagate through derived artifacts.

Publication pointer. The authoritative reference selecting a validated generation for new requests.

Q* and T*. Labels discussed in public engineer-call notes; not a disclosed complete or current scoring formula.

Query intent. An estimate of the task behind a query; ambiguous requests may require multiple hypotheses.

Query plan. A budgeted strategy for retrieval branches, shards, models, evidence collection and fallback.

Recall. The fraction of relevant items recovered; a reranker cannot rank candidates that retrieval never supplied.

Reciprocal rank fusion. Combining ranked lists by contributions based on reciprocal rank rather than incomparable raw scores.

Render budget. A cap on browser time, requests, bytes and compute while processing untrusted active content.

Replica. A copy of data or service state used for availability or read capacity under a consistency contract.

Reranking. Applying a more expensive ordering model to a candidate subset.

Robots policy. Published crawler access instructions interpreted under the relevant crawler and protocol rules.

Scope propagation. Preserving access restrictions through retrieval, features, evidence, caches, generated outputs and logs.

Segment. An immutable physical unit of index data that can be validated, replicated and merged.

Semantic support. Evidence that justifies the exact claim being made, including qualifications, dates and version boundaries.

Shard. A partition of corpus or index work; shard selection and fanout affect both recall and latency.

SLI. A precisely defined measurement of service behavior, such as valid-query success or publication freshness.

SLO. A target for an SLI over a time window; distinct from a contractual SLA.

Snapshot pinning. Keeping one request on a coherent generation instead of mixing arbitrary component versions.

Tail latency. Slow-end response behavior that can dominate requests requiring many downstream components.

Tombstone. A durable deletion or withdrawal marker that prevents old content from regaining authority accidentally.

WAND. A family of retrieval techniques using score bounds to skip work while preserving a defined top-k objective.

Writer epoch. An ownership generation checked by the destination of writes to fence an old process after failover.

APPENDIX F

Service contracts and architecture decisions

Twelve service contracts

Targets must be selected for the actual workload and risk profile. This table defines what must remain true when a dependency fails; it deliberately avoids fabricating Google's private SLOs or contract terms.

Service Authority or compatibility contract Failure mode Required behavior
Frontier Origin authority and crawl policy Source errors or overload Delay work; never evade origin limits.
Fetcher Validated destinations and byte budgets Network or parser failure Record attempt; do not invent a successful observation.
Renderer Input observation and bounded sandbox Incomplete resource loading Keep outcome explicit; avoid authoritative empty extraction.
Document store Monotonic observations and current policy Late workers or duplicates Reject stale updates; return prior identical receipts.
Index builder Immutable validated manifests Partial build or corrupt segment Retain prior published generation.
Publisher Pointer CAS and writer epoch Lost acknowledgment or failover Resolve receipt; fence obsolete ownership.
Retrieval Pinned generation and exact score contract Slow or missing shard Use documented coverage and fallback behavior.
Ranker Model-feature compatibility Inference timeout or regression Use evaluated smaller cascade.
Policy service Current authorized eligibility Unavailable or stale decision Conservative behavior for the affected surface.
Answer service Evidence, scope and support Withdrawn or contradictory evidence Rebuild, qualify, fall back or omit unsupported claims.
Cache Dependency and scope binding Policy, model or source change Invalidate affected artifacts; do not rely only on TTL.
Analytics Versioned definitions and privacy bounds Late, duplicate or deleted data Deduplicate, revise and propagate deletion appropriately.

Twelve architecture decisions

ADR-01: Immutable content, mutable pointer

Makes staged validation and rollback inspectable. Costs extra storage and requires garbage collection based on references and retention.

ADR-02: Separate current policy from index snapshots

Lets removals overtake slow rebuilds. Adds a critical serving dependency that needs its own freshness and failure contract.

ADR-03: Document partitioning as the baseline

Keeps most document-local work together and gives a clear serving model. Wide query fanout and hot partitions still require mitigation.

ADR-04: Lexical baseline before semantic expansion

Provides an exact-match safety net and understandable evaluation reference. Semantic models remain valuable but add compatibility and recall tradeoffs.

ADR-05: Versioned models, features and tokenizers

Prevents silent format mismatches. Requires release manifests, storage overlap and coordinated rollback rather than one binary switch.

ADR-06: At-least-once delivery with transactional effects

Makes uncertain acknowledgments manageable. Requires durable receipts and does not magically deduplicate unrelated external side effects.

ADR-07: Bounded per-origin acquisition

Protects sources and internal budgets. Sacrifices immediate freshness when an origin cannot safely support more work.

ADR-08: Explicit partial-coverage responses

Avoids presenting incomplete results as exhaustive. Requires product and API support for useful degradation.

ADR-09: Private scope as data lineage

Prevents accidental reuse through vectors, caches and answers. Adds access checks and reduces shared-cache efficiency.

ADR-10: Grounded synthesis as an optional stage

Preserves useful search when synthesis is unsafe or unavailable. Requires careful product handling of fallback rather than forced answers.

ADR-11: Evidence-driven rollout

Connects deployment to relevance, latency, policy and support metrics. Requires representative evaluation data and slows unsupported changes.

ADR-12: Rehearsed recovery over nominal redundancy

Tests that old content cannot regain authority after restoration. Costs capacity and operational effort beyond keeping extra replicas.

Review discipline

Record the rejected alternative, assumptions and evidence that could change each decision. A design decision is not permanent merely because it appears in a playbook. Revisit it when corpus scale, source permissions, latency requirements or team capability change. Preserve the invariant while allowing a different implementation.

APPENDIX G

Executable companion and measured results

What was actually executed

The companion contains 67 passing local unittest tests: 34 control-plane tests, 14 retrieval tests and 19 graph, metric and evidence tests. The seeded pruning-equivalence test additionally compares 160 generated query/filter configurations across four block sizes. These are assertions in one test method, not 160 separately counted test cases.

The tests exercise selected local epoch checks, monotonic observations, publication CAS, rollback, removal overlays, concurrent duplicate requests, outbox effects, positional matching, BM25, block-bound pruning, PageRank, fusion, metrics and evidence-reference validation. The test log is included in the bundle. A successful result means this version passed those local assertions; it is not a certification of a production system.

Run the lab

cd lab
python -m unittest -v
python run_experiments.py

The code uses the Python standard library and is intended for Python 3.10 or newer. The first command creates temporary SQLite databases, including tests with competing threads. The second writes experiment_results.json and schema.sql. No network access, Google account, API key or source-data download is required.

Six measured synthetic retrieval cases

Every corpus contains 1,024 documents and requests the top ten results for needle. One corpus groups matching documents near the beginning; the other mixes terms with a fixed random seed. The exhaustive baseline and bounded method returned identical ordered top-k results in all six cases.

Corpus Block size Exact documents scored Bounded documents scored Blocks skipped
separated 8 1024 32 124
separated 32 1024 32 31
separated 128 1024 128 7
mixed 8 1024 256 96
mixed 32 1024 608 13
mixed 128 1024 896 1

These counts measure document scoring, not total CPU or wall-clock speed. Index construction and the toy implementation's precomputed per-term bounds are excluded. A larger block reduces metadata work but can weaken pruning. The mixed corpus demonstrates why a correct optimization may save much less work on a different distribution. This is a simplified block-bound algorithm, not a complete production WAND iterator.

Reproduce the worked mathematics

The three-document BM25 example returns D1 with approximately 0.9400 and D2/D3 with approximately 0.4700 for red fox. The PageRank experiment includes a dangling node and a disconnected node and checks normalized nonnegative mass. The metric example produces a non-perfect nDCG when the lower-graded document precedes the higher-graded one. These are transparent teaching examples, not relevance measurements for Google Search.

Boundaries of the evidence checker

The local evidence gate verifies reference existence, a content hash, a boolean eligibility flag, expiration and an exact public/user scope. It rejects anonymous access to private scopes. It does not determine whether prose is true, whether a citation entails a claim, or whether a source is reliable. It does not implement a real permission service, administrative authorization, secure credential handling or a production policy taxonomy.

Boundaries of the transaction model

SQLite serializes local writers. The model does not prove multi-region consensus, lease safety under real clock skew, availability during partitions or durability on failed hardware. Time and caller authority are injected into teaching APIs. A production implementation must derive them from trusted infrastructure and authenticate every operation.

The ten tables deliberately omit most entities in Appendix A. Directly modifying validated rows through privileged SQL can bypass the model's intended API discipline; a production storage boundary needs permissions, immutability controls and defense in depth. Snapshot content and current policy remain separate concepts even when both reside in one local file for teaching.

A practical learning progression

First inspect the index and reproduce scores by hand. Then change block size and corpus order, add new phrase cases, and deliberately break a score bound to observe why equivalence tests matter. Next run the competing publication and policy updates. Finally add a new policy surface or a second model generation, writing the compatibility and removal tests before changing the schema.

For a deployable prototype, replace the in-memory retrieval maps with a mature index library, add real authorization and guarded fetching, and build an evaluation corpus. Introduce distributed storage only when the invariants are explicit enough to test under its actual consistency model.
